title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strengthened Skills and Transparency in the Mining sector in Rwanda

description.narrative: This action is a component of the EU-Rwanda Strategic Partnership on Sustainable Raw Materials Value Chains which foresees comprehensive and overarching collaboration articulated through a roadmap, currently in progress. It will address the pillars on sustainable and responsible raw materials production as well as training and skills development. It supports the Government¿s vision to modernise the mining sector and become a hub of transformation based on formal regional value chains, and higher environmental, labour, transparency, and traceability standards, ensuring that minerals are sourced responsibly and can be tracked throughout the supply chain. Aid to Environment will be a significant objective prioritising concrete actions such as reducing pollution, promoting sustainable resource extraction, implementing waste management systems, and ensuring the use of environmentally friendly technologies, with measurable goals to protect ecosystems, preserve biodiversity, and support climate resilience in the long term.This action aims to contribute to unlocking significant bottlenecks preventing Rwanda from unleashing its mining potential through two components: (1) addressing the shortage of skilled labour in mining and (2) consolidating and enhancing Rwanda¿s progress in mineral transparency and traceability.Moreover, the EU support will contribute to implementing the priority areas of Rwanda's Second National Strategy for Transformation (NST-2) 2024-2029 by enhancing decent job creation and export promotion. By enhancing decent job creation, the EU aims to support the development of high-quality, formal employment opportunities within the mining sector, ensuring that workers are protected by fair labour standards, safety protocols, and access to social security. Finally, this action is aligned with the Country Level Implementation Plan (CLIP) of Rwanda, especially to the objectives related to the parts III, IV and V and to the GAP III key thematic areas of engagement linked with these parts.
